resources.string: Set the app up for your trade
Everything works offline. Pick a language and your trades, and your tool and material lists are ready.
Choose one or more. You can change this later in Settings.
Nothing listed yet. Add what this job needs.
Photograph the drawing on the wall, or pick a plan someone sent you.
That image could not be saved
For work the app does not cover yet — roofing, landscaping, glazing. It starts empty and you add your own items to it.
No task list and no materials — a job you fill in yourself.
You are on the latest version
Could not check for updates. Try again when you have a signal.
Android will ask you to allow this app to install updates. That permission is only used for this app\'s own updates.
A critical item is not done. Work must not start.
Standard references are a pointer for the site file. They do not replace the published text of the standard or regulation.
Adds catalogue items that are missing. Your own items and quantities are never touched.
Used to photograph items and site progress, and to scan barcodes. Photos stay on this device unless you sync.
Optional. Stamps check-ins, site photos and incident reports with where they happened. The app works fully without it.
Used only while you dictate a task note in Hebrew or Arabic.
Reminders for scheduled tasks and low stock.
Everything stays on this phone and works with no signal. You can add people later.
One person, your own tools and jobs.
Several people, each seeing the part of the work that is theirs.
Goes on invoices. You can add it later.
At least 4 digits. Leave empty for no passcode.
There has to be one owner left, or nobody can reach the company\'s data.
Only you so far. Add the people who work with you.
Everything, including who else is here.
Runs the jobs. Sees costs, does not change them.
The money work. Does not see the schedule.
Does the work and records it.
Priced materials on the job sheet, not yet bought.
Nothing spent on this job yet.
Extra work, or work taken away. A negative amount is an omission.
DD/MM/YYYY. Leave empty if it does not expire.
No plant on the books. Add what you own or hire.
No orders yet. Raise one when you order materials.
A draft costs nothing. Place it and it counts against the job.
No version has been published yet.
No talks recorded. A briefing nobody wrote down did not happen.
Nobody has signed in. A talk with an empty register records nothing.
Everybody has been briefed this quarter.
No permits. Raise one before hot work, height, a confined space, digging or an isolation.
Every precaution has to be ticked before this permit can be issued.
The end has to come after the start.
Area left safe — anything to note
This permit has run out. It authorises nothing. Sign it back once the area is safe.
Fire extinguisher within reach of the work
Combustibles cleared or covered within 10 metres
Fire watch during the work and for 30 minutes after
Gas cylinders upright and secured, hoses checked
Anchor point checked and rated for the load
Edge protection or fall arrest in place
The area below is closed off
Rescue plan agreed and the equipment is on site
Edge barriers up and a ladder for access
Spoil and plant kept back from the edge
Proved dead with a tester proved before and after
Warning notice fitted at the isolation point
Keys held by the person doing the work
Whichever your site office gave you. Both work.
What you will type to sign in. Short is better on a site.
How the site reaches you. Required.
That is not a phone number.
That is too short to be a phone number.
That is longer than any phone number.
A number somebody can actually be reached on.
That does not look like an email address.
Leave blank if you were not given one.
That does not match. Check with whoever set you up.
Teudat Zehut or passport. Names on a site repeat; this does not.
Somebody is already signed up with that ID number.
Read this, then sign. It takes a minute, and it is the only thing on this phone that can stop you getting hurt.
Read this, then sign. All of it is also what you are about to enforce on everybody else.
So the site office can put a face to the name at the gate.
Kept on this device only. It never leaves the phone.
Sign to say you have read it
I have read this — let me in
Sign above before you can continue.
On site, always. On your head, not in your hand.
Reflective, whatever the colour. A plant driver sees the jacket before they see you, and after dark they see nothing else.
Steel toe and a protected sole. A nail goes through a trainer without slowing down.
For the job in hand: cut-resistant near blades, insulated in the cold. Never near a turning bit — a glove that catches takes the hand with it.
Cutting, grinding, drilling, chasing, and anything at all above your head.
Breakers and cut-off saws. Hearing does not come back.
If it is not safe, stop
Stop and say so. Nobody on this job is in trouble for stopping work.
First-aid kit and assembly point — find them today, not on the day you need them.
The kit above is yours to enforce
Somebody on your site without a hard hat is your problem, not theirs.
Hot work, height, confined space, excavation, isolation: no permit, no work. Issue one only when every precaution is ticked, and sign it back yourself once the area is safe.
Brief before the work, not after it. Keep the register — a briefing nobody wrote down did not happen.
Nobody works at height or operates plant on a lapsed ticket. The app warns you thirty days out — act then, not on the day.
Report the same day. Photograph it first and tidy up after — an investigation starts from what was actually there.
Ambulance 101. Fire 102. Know your assembly point and who your first aider is before the day you need them.
You can be on more than one firm\'s books. This decides whose jobs you see and what you may do.
Jobs that belong to nobody but you.
A new firm on the same phone, with its own jobs and its own crew. Your ID, photograph and induction come with you.
You are not on any firm\'s books.
No snags. Raise one when you find a defect.
Who has to put it right
Leave this off for something worth fixing that does not hold up a building.
Somebody said this was done. It stays on the list until somebody else has looked.
I have not been given an account
Set once and kept. The site office identifies you by this, so it is not something to change quietly.
You have no ID number yet, so you can only sign in with your username. Add one and either will work.
No days logged yet. Today\'s is ready when you are.
Counted from what was actually entered. Correct the entry and this corrects itself.
Nothing was recorded on this job today. If work happened, it did not reach the app.
Delays, visitors, anything an inspector or a solicitor would want to know later.
Signed and closed. A daily log that can be tidied up afterwards is evidence of nothing.
Draw a signature before signing the day off.
Trucks on the way, and how long each load has left.
No pours recorded. Start one before the first truck arrives.
As the engineer specified: B-30, and so on.
Thirty degrees or more cuts every load\'s working life from 90 minutes to 60.
Read the time off the delivery note and count back to now. The clock starts at the plant, not when the truck reached you.
Out of time — do not pour
Recorded because it cannot be seen afterwards. The engineer should know.
The seven-day register, and which ones may be climbed today.
In the words somebody would use on the radio: north elevation, stairwell 2.
Moved, added to, or hit by weather. It comes out of use until it is inspected again.
Out of date — do not climb
Changed since it was passed — do not climb
Every scaffold on this job is in date.
Lift plans, and what has to be right before the load leaves the ground.
In the words used on the radio: air handling unit, roof beam 4.
Slings, shackles, spreader beam, hook block. They hang off the same rope, and leaving them out is how a lift planned at ninety per cent turns out to have been at a hundred and four.
This appliance needs a periodic test
Off the duty chart at the radius being worked. Not the crane\'s headline tonnage.
Over three quarters of the chart — have somebody senior look at this.
Nobody has said what it weighs
No capacity from the duty chart
The appliance\'s test certificate is not in date
Propping and formwork: what may take load, and what may come down.
Props to the level 3 slab; façade retention to the north wall.
How hard it has to be checked
Standard solution, used within its limits
Simple design, checked inside the team
Checked by somebody outside the design
Somebody has held the drawing up against what is standing there. This is a separate act from building it, because the commonest failure is a good design built differently.
The decision that drops slabs. It is recorded with a name because afterwards the question is always who released it.
Days before it may be struck
The engineer\'s number, off the design. The app defaults to fourteen because that errs towards leaving props in; it does not work the figure out and it is not a judgement about the concrete.
The design has not been checked
At this level the designer cannot check his own work
Nobody has checked it was built as drawn
It has already been taken down
The concrete has not had its days
Trenches: what is buried there, and who may go in today.
In the words used on the radio: along the north boundary, grid B4.

At one metre twenty the sides have to be held back somehow. Ground collapses at less than that too — this is the depth below which nobody is required to have decided, not the depth below which nothing can happen.

Drawings from the utility, a cable scan, trial holes. The one thing on this screen that cannot be put right afterwards: a trench cut too steep can be battered back, but a cable that has been cut has been cut.
Rain, a collapse, vibration, a load put near the edge. It comes out of use until somebody has looked again.
Nobody has found out what is buried here
Deep enough to need the sides held, and nothing is holding them
Something has changed it since the last inspection

Hot work fires mostly start after the torch goes out, from a spark that fell into a void an hour ago and has been smouldering since. Somebody stays and watches; the permit cannot be signed back until they have.
What has been claimed, what was agreed, and when the money is due.
Claimed, for all work to date

The total the work is worth at this point in the job, not what was done this month. That is how applications are written, and paying the figure on the face of each one in turn pays for the same work twice.
Agreed, for all work to date
The applications before this one certified more than the work turned out to be worth. It has to come back one way or another, so the screen says so rather than showing nothing.
Shotef plus counts from the end of the month the invoice falls in, not from the invoice date. An invoice on the 3rd of March under shotef+30 is due on the 30th of April.
What is actually agreed, which need not be what was claimed. The difference between the two is the conversation, so both are kept.
Released when the defects period ends
Hours clocked on this job, and what they came to.
Nobody has clocked any hours on this job.
Hours appear here once somebody has clocked out of a shift.
These two do not agree. They are two accounts of the same money, so the app keeps them apart rather than adding them — the gap is either hours nobody costed or a cost line nobody worked.
Some days have no hourly rate against them and are not counted.
Part of these hours has no rate, so this figure is short.
What is still open across the whole job, and the pack to hand over.
Every register on this job is clear. The pack can go out as a final one.

The pack still prints, because an interim one is a real thing — a client asks for the file at the end of a phase, or a subcontractor leaves and wants their part of it. It records what was outstanding at the moment it was produced, so it reads as interim rather than looking final.
Israel edition — built to Israeli standards, terms and site rules
No work packages on this job yet
A crew sent back with no reason has nothing to fix.
Approval happens in an office days later, by which time the wall is plastered.
Approved. Not paid — the application still has to run its terms.
Only the other side can do that
Off means only management sees it. Nothing is published unless you turn it on.
Recording a licence marks you verified on this app. It is not a statement that you are licensed to do the work — that is between you and the regulator.
What your firm is on this job, which is not what it is on the next one.
What was handed out and what was taken on
Bring a firm onto the job
What they are here to do
Your position on this job cannot bring that one on.
What is your firm on this job?
Answer before anything else. Nobody else can say this for you, and until it is answered you cannot bring another firm on.
No contracts on this job yet
What was agreed, and with whom
Not signed by both sides yet
Somebody will ask in three years why this contract is worth what it is worth, and they were not there.
Every figure this contract has been
You proposed this. The other side accepts or refuses it.
What you are paid, less what you pay out. Only you can see this — it is not on anybody else’s screen.
Everything approved to date, not just what is being added. What is actually due is that less retention and less what has already been paid.
Nothing new approved since the last application
Optional. Worth setting when the same task repeats on several floors — the stage is what tells them apart.
Every approved work package counted in the figure above. A claim is cumulative, so packages from earlier applications are listed again.
Raised by hand — no work packages attached.
Every change of consequence, in the order it happened. The trail cannot be edited from inside the app.
%1$d entries checked and every one adds up.
%1$d older entries carry no signature and cannot be checked. They were written before this version.
The trail does not add up
Entry %1$d says something other than what was signed.
Entry %1$d does not follow the one before it. Something was removed or replaced.
Signatures are shortened in the PDF. The CSV carries them in full, and docs/AUDIT.md says how to recompute them.
On — the records on this device are encrypted
The key is held in this device\'s secure hardware and never leaves it. The database file cannot be read off the phone.
Off — the records on this device are NOT encrypted

This device could not load the encryption library, so the app opened the records unprotected rather than refuse to start. ID numbers, photographs and signatures can be read by anyone with access to this phone\'s files. Report this device before using it for personnel data.

How long records must be kept is a legal question, and the answer differs for a payment record, a safety inspection and a worker\'s ID number. The app does not choose for you: nothing is ever deleted until you set a period, and a purge records what it removed.
Removed %1$d entries. The purge is itself recorded in the trail.
Nothing was old enough to remove.
Write it down while it is fresh, including the near misses. A near miss is the same accident with better luck.
This may have to be reported to a regulator as well as recorded here. Check your obligations — the app does not decide this for you.
There are no accounts on this phone yet. Accounts are kept on the device, so one made on another phone cannot be reached from here until the company has a server. Create an account to get started.
Records violations and incidents against named people. Sees who somebody is, never what they are paid.
Type the number from their card. Names on a site repeat; this does not.
No one has that ID number. They have to create an account before they can be added.
Leave empty for no charge. Empty and zero are not the same.
Once confirmed this cannot be changed or withdrawn, and the person it names will see it.
Draft — only you can see this
Attach a photograph or a video. A violation with a cost and nothing to show is one person\'s word.
The number on their card. Their photograph comes back with it.
Nobody has that ID number. They sign up on their own phone first, then come back.
Will be signed onto the site as: %1$s. Their rank is set afterwards by whoever engaged them.
Already signed onto this site. Nothing to do.
Hand them the phone. They sign to say they have been briefed on this site\'s safety rules.
Signing people onto the site is not one of yours. The site manager or the safety officer does it.
Attach a photograph or a video. By the time this is argued about, the ladder has been moved.
Leave it empty if nobody knows yet. Empty and zero are not the same.
That is not an amount. Leave it empty if you do not know.
This covers only the people whose pay you may see, so it is not the job\'s whole labour.
None of the hours on this job are yours to price.
You see the pay of the people who answer to you, and your own. Nobody sees their own boss\'s.
Whoever someone answers to can see what they are paid. Nobody else can, including people beside them and above them.
Only somebody above them can move them, and you are not.
You cannot move yourself. Whoever you answer to does that.
That would put a circle in the chain: they are already above the person you picked.
Nobody on the books for that trade.
Nothing about pay here. Only somebody above them in the chain of command sees that.
Everything is on this phone and nothing is on a server. Lose the phone and you lose the site diary, unless you have a backup.
Working. This takes a while, because the photographs go in too.
Backed up, with %1$d photographs and videos. Keep the file somewhere that is not this phone.
Ready to restore the backup from %1$s. Close the app completely and open it again to finish. Nothing has changed yet.
It was taken by an older version. It will be brought up to date as it is restored.
That is not a backup from this app.
That backup was made by a newer version of the app. Update first, then restore it.
The restore did not finish, and everything you had is still here. Try again.
That did not work. Either the passphrase is wrong or the file is damaged.
Write this down somewhere safe. Nobody can reset it, and without it the backup cannot be opened by anyone, including us.
At least 12 characters. This locks a file somebody could copy and take away.
Too few different characters. Length alone is not strength.
Taken %1$s: %2$d jobs, %3$d people, %4$d photographs and videos.
The file opened but the database inside it is damaged. Do not rely on this one — take a fresh backup.
